You are reverse-engineering the behavior of a compiled binary at /workspace/executable (call it as ./executable from /workspace).
It is "gomplate", a Go text/template renderer. Documentation lives in /workspace/docs/content/.

HARD RULES (violating them fails the whole project):
- You MUST NOT use the network, MUST NOT search the web, MUST NOT download or read the original gomplate source from anywhere.
- You MUST NOT decompile, disassemble, objdump, strace, ltrace, nm, strings(1), or otherwise statically analyze ./executable.
- You may ONLY run ./executable with normal CLI arguments and observe stdout/stderr/exit code, and read the bundled docs.

How to invoke: ./executable -i '<template>'   (prints rendered result to stdout)
Errors are logged to stderr as JSON: {"time":...,"level":"ERROR","msg":"","err":"..."} and exit code 1.
Useful trick: wrap results with printf "%T / %#v" to learn the concrete Go type a function returns, e.g.
  ./executable -i '{{ printf "%T" (conv.ToInt "5") }}'
Another: {{ test.Kind x }} and {{ test.IsKind "int" x }} reveal reflect kinds.

YOUR OUTPUT: write a thorough markdown spec file. Be exhaustive and precise: this spec is the ONLY thing a
separate implementer agent will see — they will not have access to the binary at first. Every fact must be
concrete and verified by an actual command you ran.

For EVERY function in your assigned area document:
1. Exact name(s) including aliases (verify each alias actually exists in THIS build — docs are stale, some
   documented functions were removed; e.g. conv.Bool does NOT exist here).
2. Exact parameter order and count, including variadic behavior and gomplate's "data is the LAST argument"
   pipeline convention. Verify by experiment, not by reading docs.
3. The concrete Go return type (use printf "%T").
4. Type coercion rules for inputs (what happens with int vs string vs float vs bool vs nil vs slice vs map).
5. Error messages VERBATIM (copy the exact "err" string), and whether it errors vs returns zero value.
6. Edge cases: empty string, empty slice, nil, negative numbers, unicode/multibyte, very large numbers,
   wrong arg count, wrong types.
7. At least 5-15 concrete verified examples per function in the form:
   | template | output |
   Use a fenced table or list. Copy outputs EXACTLY (including whitespace/newlines; note trailing newlines).

Finish the spec with a "GOTCHAS" section listing anything surprising an implementer would get wrong.
Do not summarize or truncate — length is good. Aim for a very detailed document.

YOUR ASSIGNED AREA: strings
Relevant docs: /workspace/docs/content/functions/strings.md (read it first to get the function list, then verify each against the binary).
This is the biggest namespace (29 funcs). Pay special attention to strings.Trunc/Abbrev/Indent/Slug/WordWrap/ShellQuote/Sort/SkipLines and the exact word-wrapping algorithm (test long inputs, existing newlines, and width edge cases). Also check strings.Split/SplitN return types and strings.Trim family arg order.

Write your spec to /tmp/spec/strings.md using the Write tool. Then reply with just a one-paragraph summary of what you covered and anything you could not determine.

9	## `strings.Abbrev`
10	
11	Abbreviates a string using `...` (ellipses). Takes an optional offset from the beginning of the string, and a maximum final width (including added ellipses).
12	
13	_Also see [`strings.Trunc`](#stringstrunc)._
14	
15	_Added in gomplate [v2.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.6.0)_
16	### Usage
17	
18	```
19	strings.Abbrev [offset] width input
20	```
21	```
22	input | strings.Abbrev [offset] width
23	```
24	
25	### Arguments
26	
27	| name | description |
28	|------|-------------|
29	| `offset` | _(optional)_ offset from the start of the string. Must be `4` or greater for ellipses to be added. Defaults to `0` |
30	| `width` | _(required)_ the desired maximum final width of the string, including ellipses |
31	| `input` | _(required)_ the input string to abbreviate |
32	
33	### Examples
34	
35	```console
36	$ gomplate -i '{{ "foobarbazquxquux" | strings.Abbrev 9 }}'
37	foobar...
38	$ gomplate -i '{{ "foobarbazquxquux" | strings.Abbrev 6 9 }}'
39	...baz...
40	```
41	
42	## `strings.Contains`
43	
44	Reports whether a substring is contained within a string.
45	
46	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
47	### Usage
48	
49	```
50	strings.Contains substr input
51	```
52	```
53	input | strings.Contains substr
54	```
55	
56	### Arguments
57	
58	| name | description |
59	|------|-------------|
60	| `substr` | _(required)_ the substring to search for |
61	| `input` | _(required)_ the input to search |
62	
63	### Examples
64	
65	_`input.tmpl`:_
66	```
67	{{ if (env.Getenv "FOO" | strings.Contains "f") }}yes{{else}}no{{end}}
68	```
69	
70	```console
71	$ FOO=foo gomplate < input.tmpl
72	yes
73	$ FOO=bar gomplate < input.tmpl
74	no
75	```

77	## `strings.HasPrefix`
78	
79	Tests whether a string begins with a certain prefix.
80	
81	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
82	### Usage
83	
84	```
85	strings.HasPrefix prefix input
86	```
87	```
88	input | strings.HasPrefix prefix
89	```
90	
91	### Arguments
92	
93	| name | description |
94	|------|-------------|
95	| `prefix` | _(required)_ the prefix to search for |
96	| `input` | _(required)_ the input to search |
97	
98	### Examples
99	
100	```console
101	$ URL=http://example.com gomplate -i '{{if env.Env.URL | strings.HasPrefix "https"}}foo{{else}}bar{{end}}'
102	bar
103	$ URL=https://example.com gomplate -i '{{if env.Env.URL | strings.HasPrefix "https"}}foo{{else}}bar{{end}}'
104	foo
105	```

107	## `strings.HasSuffix`
108	
109	Tests whether a string ends with a certain suffix.
110	
111	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
112	### Usage
113	
114	```
115	strings.HasSuffix suffix input
116	```
117	```
118	input | strings.HasSuffix suffix
119	```
120	
121	### Arguments
122	
123	| name | description |
124	|------|-------------|
125	| `suffix` | _(required)_ the suffix to search for |
126	| `input` | _(required)_ the input to search |
127	
128	### Examples
129	
130	_`input.tmpl`:_
131	```
132	{{env.Env.URL}}{{if not (env.Env.URL | strings.HasSuffix ":80")}}:80{{end}}
133	```
134	
135	```console
136	$ URL=http://example.com gomplate < input.tmpl
137	http://example.com:80
138	```

140	## `strings.Indent`
141	
142	**Alias:** `indent`
143	
144	Indents a string. If the input string has multiple lines, each line will be indented.
145	
146	As of v4.0.0, this function will error if the `width` or `indent` arguments are invalid.
147	
148	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
149	### Usage
150	
151	```
152	strings.Indent [width] [indent] input
153	```
154	```
155	input | strings.Indent [width] [indent]
156	```
157	
158	### Arguments
159	
160	| name | description |
161	|------|-------------|
162	| `width` | _(optional)_ Number of times to repeat the `indent` string. Must be greater than 0. Default: `1` |
163	| `indent` | _(optional)_ The string to indent with. Must not contain a newline character ("\n"). Default: `" "` |
164	| `input` | _(required)_ The string to indent |
165	
166	### Examples
167	
168	This function can be especially useful when adding YAML snippets into other YAML documents, where indentation is important:
169	
170	_`input.tmpl`:_
171	```
172	foo:
173	{{ `{"bar": {"baz": 2}}` | json | toYAML | strings.Indent "  " }}
174	{{- `{"qux": true}` | json | toYAML | strings.Indent 2 }}
175	  quux:
176	{{ `{"quuz": 42}` | json | toYAML | strings.Indent 2 "  " -}}
177	```
178	
179	```console
180	$ gomplate -f input.tmpl
181	foo:
182	  bar:
183	    baz: 2
184	  qux: true
185	
186	  quux:
187	    quuz: 42
188	```

190	## `strings.SkipLines`
191	
192	Skips the given number of lines (each ending in a `\n`), returning the
193	remainder.
194	
195	If `skip` is greater than the number of lines in `in`, an empty string is
196	returned.
197	
198	_Added in gomplate [v4.0.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v4.0.0)_
199	### Usage
200	
201	```
202	strings.SkipLines skip in
203	```
204	```
205	in | strings.SkipLines skip
206	```
207	
208	### Arguments
209	
210	| name | description |
211	|------|-------------|
212	| `skip` | _(required)_ the number of lines to skip - must be a positive number |
213	| `in` | _(required)_ the input string |
214	
215	### Examples
216	
217	```console
218	$ gomplate -i '{{ "foo\nbar\nbaz" | strings.SkipLines 2 }}'
219	baz
220	```
221	```console
222	$ gomplate -i '{{ strings.SkipLines 1 "foo\nbar\nbaz" }}'
223	bar
224	baz
225	```

227	## `strings.Split`
228	
229	Slices `input` into the substrings separated by `separator`, returning a
230	slice of the substrings between those separators. If `input` does not
231	contain `separator` and `separator` is not empty, returns a single-element
232	slice whose only element is `input`.
233	
234	If `separator` is empty, it will split after each UTF-8 sequence. If
235	both inputs are empty (i.e. `strings.Split "" ""`), it will return an
236	empty slice.
237	
238	This is equivalent to [`strings.SplitN`](#stringssplitn) with a `count`
239	of `-1`.
240	
241	Note that the delimiter is not included in the resulting elements.
242	
243	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
244	### Usage
245	
246	```
247	strings.Split separator input
248	```
249	```
250	input | strings.Split separator
251	```
252	
253	### Arguments
254	
255	| name | description |
256	|------|-------------|
257	| `separator` | _(required)_ the delimiter to split on, can be multiple characters |
258	| `input` | _(required)_ the input string |
259	
260	### Examples
261	
262	```console
263	$ gomplate -i '{{range ("Bart,Lisa,Maggie" | strings.Split ",") }}Hello, {{.}}
264	{{end}}'
265	Hello, Bart
266	Hello, Lisa
267	Hello, Maggie
268	```
269	```console
270	$ gomplate -i '{{range strings.Split "," "One,Two,Three" }}{{.}}{{"\n"}}{{end}}'
271	One
272	Two
273	Three
274	```
275	
276	## `strings.SplitN`
277	
278	Slices `input` into the substrings separated by `separator`, returning a
279	slice of the substrings between those separators. If `input` does not
280	contain `separator` and `separator` is not empty, returns a single-element
281	slice whose only element is `input`.
282	
283	The `count` determines the number of substrings to return:
284	
285	* `count > 0`: at most `count` substrings; the last substring will be the
286	  unsplit remainder.
287	* `count == 0`: the result is nil (zero substrings)
288	* `count < 0`: all substrings
289	
290	See [`strings.Split`](#stringssplit) for more details.
291	
292	_Added in gomplate [v1.9.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v1.9.0)_
293	### Usage
294	
295	```
296	strings.SplitN separator count input
297	```
298	```
299	input | strings.SplitN separator count
300	```
301	
302	### Arguments
303	
304	| name | description |
305	|------|-------------|
306	| `separator` | _(required)_ the delimiter to split on, can be multiple characters |
307	| `count` | _(required)_ the maximum number of substrings to return |
308	| `input` | _(required)_ the input string |
309	
310	### Examples
311	
312	```console
313	$ gomplate -i '{{ range ("foo:bar:baz" | strings.SplitN ":" 2) }}{{.}}
314	{{end}}'
315	foo
316	bar:baz
317	```

319	## `strings.Quote`
320	
321	**Alias:** `quote`
322	
323	Surrounds an input string with double-quote characters (`"`). If the input is not a string, converts first.
324	
325	`"` characters in the input are first escaped with a `\` character.
326	
327	This is a convenience function which is equivalent to:
328	
329	```
330	{{ print "%q" "input string" }}
331	```
332	
333	_Added in gomplate [v3.1.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.1.0)_
334	### Usage
335	
336	```
337	strings.Quote in
338	```
339	```
340	in | strings.Quote
341	```
342	
343	### Arguments
344	
345	| name | description |
346	|------|-------------|
347	| `in` | _(required)_ The input to quote |
348	
349	### Examples
350	
351	```console
352	$ gomplate -i '{{ "in" | quote }}'
353	"in"
354	$ gomplate -i '{{ strings.Quote 500 }}'
355	"500"
356	```

358	## `strings.Repeat`
359	
360	Returns a new string consisting of `count` copies of the input string.
361	
362	It errors if `count` is negative or if the length of `input` multiplied by `count` overflows.
363	
364	This wraps Go's [`strings.Repeat`](https://pkg.go.dev/strings/#Repeat).
365	
366	_Added in gomplate [v2.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.6.0)_
367	### Usage
368	
369	```
370	strings.Repeat count input
371	```
372	```
373	input | strings.Repeat count
374	```
375	
376	### Arguments
377	
378	| name | description |
379	|------|-------------|
380	| `count` | _(required)_ the number of times to repeat the input |
381	| `input` | _(required)_ the input to repeat |
382	
383	### Examples
384	
385	```console
386	$ gomplate -i '{{ "hello " | strings.Repeat 5 }}'
387	hello hello hello hello hello
388	```

423	## `strings.Slug`
424	
425	Creates a a "slug" from a given string - supports Unicode correctly. This wraps the [github.com/gosimple/slug](https://github.com/gosimple/slug) package. See [the github.com/gosimple/slug docs](https://pkg.go.dev/github.com/gosimple/slug) for more information.
426	
427	_Added in gomplate [v2.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v2.6.0)_
428	### Usage
429	
430	```
431	strings.Slug input
432	```
433	```
434	input | strings.Slug
435	```
436	
437	### Arguments
438	
439	| name | description |
440	|------|-------------|
441	| `input` | _(required)_ the input to "slugify" |
442	
443	### Examples
444	
445	```console
446	$ gomplate -i '{{ "Hello, world!" | strings.Slug }}'

454	## `strings.ShellQuote`
455	
456	**Alias:** `shellQuote`
457	
458	Given a string, emits a version of that string that will evaluate to its literal data when expanded by any POSIX-compliant shell.
459	
460	Given an array or slice, emit a single string which will evaluate to a series of shell words, one per item in that array or slice.
461	
462	_Added in gomplate [v3.6.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.6.0)_
463	### Usage
464	
465	```
466	strings.ShellQuote in
467	```
468	```
469	in | strings.ShellQuote
470	```
471	
472	### Arguments
473	
474	| name | description |
475	|------|-------------|
476	| `in` | _(required)_ The input to quote |
477	
478	### Examples
479	
480	```console
481	$ gomplate -i "{{ coll.Slice \"one word\" \"foo='bar baz'\" | shellQuote }}"
482	'one word' 'foo='"'"'bar baz'"'"''
483	```
484	```console
485	$ gomplate -i "{{ strings.ShellQuote \"it's a banana\" }}"
486	'it'"'"'s a banana'
487	```

894	See [Kebab Case on Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kebab_case) for more details.

923	## `strings.WordWrap`
924	
925	Inserts new line breaks into the input string so it ends up with lines that are at most `width` characters wide.
926	
927	The line-breaking algorithm is _naïve_ and _greedy_: lines are only broken between words (i.e. on whitespace characters), and no effort is made to "smooth" the line endings.
928	
929	When words that are longer than the desired width are encountered (e.g. long URLs), they are not broken up. Correctness is valued above line length.
930	
931	The line-break sequence defaults to `\n` (i.e. the LF/Line Feed character), regardless of OS.
932	
933	_Added in gomplate [v3.3.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.3.0)_
934	### Usage
935	
936	```
937	strings.WordWrap [width] [lbseq] in
938	```
939	```
940	in | strings.WordWrap [width] [lbseq]
941	```
942	
943	### Arguments
944	
945	| name | description |
946	|------|-------------|
947	| `width` | _(optional)_ The desired maximum line length (number of characters - defaults to `80`) |
948	| `lbseq` | _(optional)_ The line-break sequence to use (defaults to `\n`) |
949	| `in` | _(required)_ The input |
950	
951	### Examples
952	
953	```console
954	$ gomplate -i '{{ "Hello, World!" | strings.WordWrap 7 }}'
955	Hello,
956	World!
957	```
958	```console
959	$ gomplate -i '{{ strings.WordWrap 20 "\\\n" "a string with a long url http://example.com/a/very/long/url which should not be broken" }}'
960	a string with a long
961	url
962	http://example.com/a/very/long/url
963	which should not be
964	broken
965	```

967	## `strings.RuneCount`
968	
969	Return the number of _runes_ (Unicode code-points) contained within the
970	input. This is similar to the built-in `len` function, but `len` counts
971	the length in _bytes_. The length of an input containing multi-byte
972	code-points should therefore be measured with `strings.RuneCount`.
973	
974	Inputs will first be converted to strings, and multiple inputs are
975	concatenated.
976	
977	This wraps Go's [`utf8.RuneCountInString`](https://pkg.go.dev/unicode/utf8/#RuneCountInString)
978	function.
979	
980	_Added in gomplate [v3.4.0](https://github.com/hairyhenderson/gomplate/releases/tag/v3.4.0)_
981	### Usage
982	
983	```
984	strings.RuneCount input
985	```
986	```
987	input | strings.RuneCount
988	```
989	
990	### Arguments
991	
992	| name | description |
993	|------|-------------|
994	| `input` | _(required)_ the input(s) to measure |
995	
996	### Examples
997	
998	```console
999	$ gomplate -i '{{ range (coll.Slice "\u03a9" "\u0030" "\u1430") }}{{ printf "%s is %d bytes and %d runes\n" . (len .) (strings.RuneCount .) }}{{ end }}'
1000	Ω is 2 bytes and 1 runes
1001	0 is 1 bytes and 1 runes
1002	ᐰ is 3 bytes and 1 runes
1003	```

EOF
